suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-17 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited ten-year prospective follow-up of patients with dysthymic disorder found that nearly all developed a major depressive episode superimposed on the chronic dysthymia (double depression), establishing temporal risk rather than individual causation. Require independently established persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) and a separately documented major depressive episode superimposed upon it; the cited prospective follow-up found that most dysthymic patients developed a major depressive episode during ten years of observation; do not treat persistent depressive disorder as proof that any individual's depressive disorder was caused by it. Preserve other psychiatric illness, substance use, medical illness, medications, and shared vulnerability as competing explanations. Treat this only as population-level temporal risk, not proof that persistent depressive disorder caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
